title: Separate a cached storefront from authoritative checkout
businessContext: A fast cached product page is being used as proof that an item is still available when payment begins.
problemStatement: Design the system for 50,000 visitors/minute during a launch; inventory must never go negative. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Reserve stock atomically with bounded expiry.
Handle payment timeouts without duplicate charges.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 50,000 visitors/minute during a launch; inventory must never go negative
functional: Reserve stock atomically with bounded expiry.
Handle payment timeouts without duplicate charges.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Serve public catalog content under a measured caching policy while treating displayed availability as advisory.

The payment provider may commit a charge before the response times out. Do not release stock or create a second charge solely because the HTTP call failed; reconcile the stored order/payment attempt and handle reservation expiry with a defined compensation policy.
alternativeApproaches: It can show a pending interaction, but paid must come from an authoritative confirmed transition. Client optimism, Next.js revalidation and a disabled button cannot establish a financial outcome.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Race many buyers for the last unit in real database integration tests.
Crash between reservation, outbox delivery and provider response.
Replay provider webhooks and verify exactly-once business effects through constraints, not process memory.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
